reconstruction.text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every j in N={0,1,2,...}, the map Phi_j:E -> L^2(gamma_E; R) is twice continuously Frechet differentiable over R on the entire ambient space E. Differentiability is with respect to w and measured in the L^2 norm in the codomain.
